definition: Referring expression generation (REG) is the subtask of natural language generation (NLG) that received most scholarly attention.
details: While NLG is concerned with the conversion of non-linguistic information into natural language, REG focuses only on the creation of referring expressions (noun phrases) that identify specific entities called targets. This task can be split into two sections. The content selection part determines which set of properties distinguish the intended target and the linguistic realization part defines how these properties are translated into natural language. A variety of algorithms have been developed in the NLG community to generate different types of referring expressions.

explainer.lead: The subtask of natural language generation that creates referring expressions — noun phrases identifying specific entities called targets. It matters because it received the most scholarly attention within NLG.

tiers.eli5: When you say 'the red cup on the left' instead of just 'the cup', you're picking the words that let someone else find exactly the thing you mean.
tiers.practitioner: Split into content selection, which picks the properties distinguishing the target, and linguistic realization, which turns those properties into language; a pitfall is choosing properties that don't actually single out the target.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as the NLG subtask focused only on creating referring expressions (noun phrases) that identify specific entities called targets, split into content selection (which set of properties distinguishes the target) and linguistic realization (how those properties translate into natural language).

explainer.example: To identify one cup among several, content selection picks 'red' and 'on the left', and realization produces 'the red cup on the left'.
